local.h: $75 million raised for Bronzeville cultural zone
local.b: The Bronzeville Legacy Collective has raised $75 million toward nine cultural sites, with a long-term goal of $250 million.
more: Projects include the National Museum of Gospel Music and the Emmett Till and Mamie Till-Mobley House.
Several are expected to open between 2027 and 2029.

local.h: Runner set for his 48th Chicago Marathon
local.b: Henry Kozlowski is one of two people who have finished every Chicago Marathon since 1977, and he plans to run in his high school gym shorts.

local.h: Bob Odenkirk heads back to the stage
local.b: The Naperville native is leaning into theater, with a play in Champaign about an alien invasion up next.

local.h: Mamdani to clear 10,000 families off childcare waitlist
local.b: The city will move 10,000 low-income families off the waitlist for subsidized childcare, Mayor Mamdani announced.
more: More than 16,000 families are waiting for the Child Care Assistance Program, which serves families earning up to $116,000 a year for a family of four.
Governor Kathy Hochul is putting $475 million toward the backlog that built up since May 2025.

local.h: Two killed in Queens and Brooklyn crashes
local.b: A hit-and-run on Monday killed a 62-year-old man, and a crash involving an impaired driver on Sunday killed a 23-year-old woman, police said.

local.h: NY's stockpiled abortion pills have all expired
local.b: In 2023 the state bought 150,000 misoprostol pills, enough for 12,500 doses, for $112,000. Now they are all expired.

local.h: Legionnaires' outbreaks spark NYC water debate
local.b: A group backed by cooling tower companies wants the city to filter all drinking water; experts dispute that it is needed.

local.h: City Council hearing to spotlight AI risks

local.b: The 54-year-old was hospitalized twice after his arrest Friday, police said.
